text: Git branching is a powerful tool in version control that helps teams work on new features without disrupting the main project. When starting a new task, developers create a *feature branch* from the main codebase. This branch acts like a separate workspace where they can experiment, make changes, and commit their work safely. Once the feature is complete and tested, the next step is *merging*—integrating those changes back into the main branch. To ensure quality, teams often use *pull requests* before merging, which allow others to review the code, discuss improvements, and catch errors early. This workflow keeps the main branch stable, encourages collaboration, and makes tracking changes straightforward.
